1.title: Connectors, Skills and Keeping Configurations Current
1.text: Welcome to Module twelve: Connectors, Skills and Keeping Configurations Current. This module covers connectors, skills and keeping configurations current. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. What connectors are and what Google Drive, Gmail and Calendar connectors can do. The difference between web connectors, desktop extensions and custom connectors. How permissions and approvals protect you. What Skills are and when to use them. How to maintain and update Projects, knowledge and instructions over time.

1.title: Case Check-In: Cedarbrook's Weekly Digest
1.text: Our running case is Cedarbrook Outfitters. Cedarbrook's Weekly Digest. A project manager wants Claude to read the latest planning documents in Google Drive, check the calendar for next week's deadlines and draft an email digest. Pasting each document is slow and the files change daily; a connector brings the live content into the chat.

1.title: Connectors
1.text: Connectors. A connector lets Claude access your apps and services, retrieve data and, with approval, take actions. Claude works within your own permissions: it can only reach content you could open yourself.

1.title: Connectors, continued
1.text: Connectors, continued. The figure shows this: Connectors give Claude access to your apps within your permissions, with approvals for actions that change things.

1.title: Connectors, continued
1.text: Connectors, continued. Web (remote) connectors. What it is: Cloud services you sign into: Google Workspace, Slack, Notion, Git Hub, company apps. Where it runs: In the cloud; works on web, desktop and mobile; the default choice. Desktop extensions. What it is: Tools that run on your computer. Where it runs: Claude Desktop only; for local files, local databases, O S-level access. Custom connectors. What it is: Any service that supports M C P (Model Context Protocol), added by U R L (uniform resource locator). Where it runs: Needs a public address; only connect servers you trust; Free plans may have only one. Google Workspace connectors.

1.title: Connectors, continued
1.text: Connectors, continued. Gmail. Claude can: Search and read email, draft, manage labels; attachments: metadata only. Needs approval by default: Send, reply, forward. Google Calendar. Claude can: View events, find free time, create and update events, respond to invitations. Needs approval by default: Changes to events (per your settings). Google Drive. Claude can: Search and read Docs, Sheets, Slides, P D F s; add Docs to chats and (private) Projects; save generated files. Needs approval by default: Share, move, trash. Each action requires your explicit approval by default; users can disable individual tools; admins on Team and Enterprise decide what can run without approval. Responses cite the emails, events or documents used.

1.title: Connectors, continued
1.text: Connectors, continued. Added Google Docs sync: if the document changes, the chat or Project sees the update. Data handling: retrieved data is tied to its chat and is deleted with the chat; Anthropic does not train its models on Gmail, Drive or Calendar connector data; data is encrypted. Team and Enterprise: an owner must enable a connector for the organization, but each user still signs in individually; owners can set tool actions to Always allow, Needs approval or Blocked. Exam tip: A connector gives Claude your access, not extra access. If you cannot open a file, neither can Claude; and actions that send or change things ask for approval first.

1.title: Managing Connectors and Knowledge Well
1.text: Managing Connectors and Knowledge Well. Add. Customize greater than Connectors, or the " plus " menu in a chat; review the access requested; sign in. Turn on per chat. Use the toggles in the Connectors menu; only enable what the task needs. Tool access mode. Auto (default: Claude loads what it needs), Always available (all connectors loaded; for fewer than ten you use constantly), On demand (loaded when needed; for ten or more). Reduce clutter. Each connector uses conversation space and usage; turn off what you do not need. Remove. Disconnect services you no longer use. Fix a broken link. Disconnect and reconnect from Customize greater than Connectors.

1.title: Managing Connectors and Knowledge Well, continued
1.text: Managing Connectors and Knowledge Well, continued. Check approvals. Read the approval request before accepting an action that sends, shares or deletes. Uploaded knowledge versus a connector. Freshness. Uploaded file: A snapshot at upload time. Connector (live source): Current content (synced Docs). Control. Uploaded file: You decide exactly what Claude sees. Connector (live source): Claude can search what you can access. Best for. Uploaded file: Stable documents (policies, guides). Connector (live source): Frequently changing documents, email and calendar. Risk. Uploaded file: Goes stale. Connector (live source): Broad access: keep scope narrow. Do not connect sources you do not need. Broader access means more places for sensitive data to enter a chat (Module thirteen).

1.title: Managing Connectors and Knowledge Well, continued
1.text: Managing Connectors and Knowledge Well, continued. Research can use enabled connectors without asking each time; on mobile it may skip them. Check which are on. Shared chats that use connector content may be restricted by the organization's settings.

1.title: Skills
1.text: Skills. Skills are folders of instructions, scripts and resources that Claude loads dynamically for specialized tasks. They teach Claude a repeatable method, such as "build our weekly report in the company format".

1.title: Skills, continued
1.text: Skills, continued. The figure shows this: A skill is a folder with a short description that is always visible; the instructions and resources load only when a task needs them.

1.title: Skills, continued
1.text: Skills, continued. Progressive loading. Claude sees the short description first and loads the full instructions and files only when relevant, which prevents context overload. Types. Anthropic skills (built-in: Excel, Word, Power Point, P D F), custom skills (your own), organization skills (provisioned by Team or Enterprise owners), partner skills. Requirement. Code execution or Create and edit files must be on. Creating. A folder with a skill file that starts with a name and a description (what it does and when to use it); optional extra files; zip it (folder name matches skill name) and upload in Customize greater than Skills.

1.title: Skills, continued
1.text: Skills, continued. Good skills. One specific repeatable task, clear instructions, examples, a precise description. Sharing. Custom skills stay private until shared; Team and Enterprise can share or publish with review. Security. Install skills only from trusted sources; review bundled scripts; never put passwords or keys in a skill. Skills versus Projects versus connectors. Project. Gives Claude: Static background knowledge and instructions. Loaded: Always, inside the Project. Skill. Gives Claude: A procedure for a task. Loaded: Only when relevant, anywhere. Connector. Gives Claude: Access to data and tools. Loaded: When enabled for the chat. Exam tip: Background facts live in a Project; a repeatable method lives in a Skill; live data and actions come through a connector.

2.title: Keeping Configurations Current
2.text: Keeping Configurations Current. Configurations decay: policies change, products launch, people leave. Maintain them like any shared document.

2.title: Keeping Configurations Current, continued
2.text: Keeping Configurations Current, continued. The figure shows this: Keep configurations current: review on a schedule, update, test, inform the team and record the version.

2.title: Keeping Configurations Current, continued
2.text: Keeping Configurations Current, continued. Name an owner. One person is responsible for each Project, skill and shared prompt. Review on a schedule. For example monthly or whenever a policy changes. Replace, don't pile up. Remove old files; keep one current version; use dates or versions in filenames. Test after changes. Re-run five to ten sample questions, including tricky ones, and compare. Inform the team. Tell users what changed and why; share new best practices. Version and log. Keep a short change log of instructions and knowledge.

2.title: Keeping Configurations Current, continued
2.text: Keeping Configurations Current, continued. Watch the signals. Complaints, wrong answers and drift tell you what to fix (Module fifteen). Mind access. Remove people who left; check sharing levels; review connector scopes. Know where facts live. One source of truth, referenced by the Project, not copied in many places. When a policy changes, update the knowledge and the instructions that mention it, then test. Features and names change; check the Release notes and Help Center for new capabilities and changes. If an answer cites an outdated rule, first suspect stale knowledge, then conflicting files, then unclear instructions. Exam tip: A connector gives Claude your access, so keep the scope narrow, read approval requests, and disconnect what you no longer use.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Connectors: Claude uses your permissions; approvals for sending, sharing, changing. Types: Web (default), desktop extensions (local), custom (M C P, trusted only). Google: Gmail (attachment metadata only), Calendar, Drive (docs sync). Data: Tied to the chat; deleted with it; no training on connector data. Admins: Owner enables; each user signs in; Always allow or Needs approval or Blocked. Tool access: Auto, Always available (fewer than ten), On demand (ten or more). Skills: Folders of instructions; load when relevant; need code execution; trusted sources only. Compare: Project equals background, Skill equals procedure, Connector equals live data and actions. Maintain: Owner, schedule, replace stale files, test, tell the team, version.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. A project manager wants Claude to work with the latest versions of Google Docs that change daily. Which approach fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A. A connector reaches current content; static uploads go stale.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. What can Claude access through the Gmail connector? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A. Connectors operate within your own permissions, with approval for actions such as sending.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. A team has twelve connectors enabled and chats hit length limits. What is the best adjustment? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A. Each connector uses conversation space; keep only what the task needs.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. Which item belongs in a Skill rather than a Project? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B. A skill packages a procedure that loads only when relevant.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. A shared Skill comes from an unknown website. What should you do before enabling it? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B. Skills can include scripts; install only from trusted sources and review them.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. Select two. Which two are good practices for keeping a Project current? The five options are on the screen. The answers are A and D. Replacing stale material and testing with sample questions after each change keep a Project accurate as policies and products change.

2.title: Practice Question 7
2.text: Question seven. After the return window changed from thirty to fourteen days, the assistant still says thirty. What is the most likely cause? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C. When an answer cites an outdated rule, first check the knowledge files and instructions for the old value before suspecting the model.

2.title: Practice Question 8
2.text: Question eight. An owner enabled the Google Drive connector for the organization. A new employee opens Claude. What is true? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B. Owners enable connectors, but each user authenticates and keeps their own permissions.

2.title: Practice Question 9
2.text: Question nine. Which source is a desktop extension best suited to? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D. Desktop extensions run on your computer through Claude Desktop, which suits local files and tools that have no cloud version.

2.title: Answers at a Glance
2.text: Here are all nine answers. Question one: A. Question two: A. Question three: A. Question four: B. Question five: B. Question six: A and D. Question seven: C. Question eight: B. Question nine: D. In the next module, we continue the course.
